stories.title: Meta wants your next gadget to be Muse-infused
stories.simple_summary: Meta is giving away free code so that other companies can put its AI assistant called Muse into devices like TVs and toasters.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to tech companies and gadget makers right now — there's nothing you need to do, but eventually you might see AI show up in more of your home devices.

stories.title: Trump expected to name intelligence chief Jay Clayton as new AI czar
stories.simple_summary: The president is expected to appoint Jay Clayton to lead the government's AI policy.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and policy watchers — it's about government decisions, not something that directly affects your daily life or business.

stories.title: OpenAI investigating other potential AI hacking incidents after Hugging Face breach
stories.simple_summary: OpenAI discovered that hackers may have broken into some of their systems, and they're investigating whether other security breaches happened too.
stories.why_it_matters: If you use OpenAI tools for your business, this is a reminder to be cautious about what information you share with AI services — keep your sensitive business data private.

stories.title: Sean Parker is rebuilding Stability AI around music
stories.simple_summary: Sean Parker (a famous tech entrepreneur) is starting a new company that uses AI to create music, and the music industry is supporting him this time.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to music industry investors and creators — ordinary people don't need to act on this unless you're directly involved in making or distributing music.

stories.title: Meta open sources code to let you make Muse AI gadgets
stories.simple_summary: Meta is letting anyone download free code to build their own gadgets with Muse AI, like a reminder screen or a TV stick.
stories.why_it_matters: If you're a tech hobbyist or small electronics maker, you now have a free tool to experiment with — otherwise, this is just what companies might use to build gadgets you'll eventually buy.

stories.title: The Powerful Yet Fragile Force Propping Up Stocks and the Economy
stories.simple_summary: The New York Times article headline suggests something is keeping stock prices and the economy stable, but details aren't clear from the headline alone.
stories.why_it_matters: Without knowing what the article actually says, we can't tell you what this means — read the full story if you're interested in how investments are doing.

stories.title: Apple will limit Mac disk access as AI agents ‘substantially’ increase risk
stories.simple_summary: Apple is making it harder for AI programs to access everything on your Mac computer to protect your privacy and safety.
stories.why_it_matters: If you use a Mac, this is good news — it means Apple is being more careful to stop AI programs from secretly looking at all your files, emails, and browsing history.

stories.title: Prediction: This Artificial Intelligence (AI) Chip Stock Will Make a Big Move in October (Hint: It’s Not Micron)
stories.simple_summary: An investment newsletter is predicting that a certain AI chip company's stock will move up soon.
stories.why_it_matters: This is purely for stock investors — it's speculation about which company's shares might go up, nothing that affects ordinary business owners or people.

stories.title: Affected by layoffs? Don’t miss this $75 deal for your TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 Expo+ Pass
stories.simple_summary: TechCrunch is offering a discounted ticket to a tech conference for people who lost their jobs.
stories.why_it_matters: This is only relevant if you were recently laid off and looking for a networking event or job opportunity — otherwise you can skip this.

stories.title: Apple says it’s tightening macOS ‘Full Disk Access’ controls due to new risks from AI agents
stories.simple_summary: Apple is adding extra safety controls on Mac computers to prevent AI programs from having access to too much personal information like your emails and browsing history.
stories.why_it_matters: If you use a Mac, this protects your privacy — it makes it harder for AI to secretly read your private files and personal messages.

stories.title: OpenAI’s Dot agent is enterprise software that can also order your dinner
stories.simple_summary: OpenAI made a new AI system called Dots that can do office work tasks for companies and can also do personal things like order food.
stories.why_it_matters: If you run a business, this shows that AI tools for handling paperwork and schedules are getting more capable — you might consider whether they could help your business someday.

stories.title: Call it AI, call it Super Intelligence, only 2% of consumers are buying it
stories.simple_summary: Even though the government and tech companies are promoting AI heavily, surveys show only 2% of regular people are actually buying into the excitement.
stories.why_it_matters: This honestly just means that most people like you aren't convinced yet that AI is necessary in their lives — you're not alone if you're skeptical or waiting to see what actually works.
